topic: The IKEA effect: why you overvalue what you build
title: Why You Overvalue What You Build Yourself
voiceover: Why do you love things you built yourself? Michael Norton, Daniel Mochon and Dan Ariely call it the IKEA effect. In four studies, people assembled IKEA boxes, folded origami and built Lego sets. They valued their own creations more than similar products they hadn't made. Participants also saw their amateur creations as similar in value to experts' creations. And they expected other people to share their opinion. In another study, the effect held even for simple boxes that couldn't be customized. But the effect disappeared when people failed to finish building, or when their creation was destroyed. So when you've built something, ask how much of your attachment comes from the effort. Tomorrow: does time really speed up as you get older?

accuracy_note: Findings come from lab studies with IKEA boxes, origami and Lego. The 'would you pay 63% more' figure sometimes quoted online was not verified and is not used.
